text.tspan: Hands cultivate a garden with care.
There is more than one way to care for a plant. In my experience, practical preparation and attention to
others are two useful starting points.
One reason is that observing a plant helps us respond to what it needs. For instance, we check whether
the soil feels dry before adding water. This prevents a small difficulty from taking over the experience. It
also leaves us more time to notice what is happening.
Another reason is that keeping a simple record helps us learn from changes. For example, we note
which window gives the plant enough light without scorching its leaves. This approach recognises that
the experience belongs to more than one person and that different people may need different things.
These examples show why preparation and consideration work well together. We do not have to control
every detail. We can make a sensible arrangement and remain ready to respond.
BUILD YOUR OWN · State a focused main idea. Develop one supporting reason in each body paragraph, with a concrete
example. Conclude by connecting the two reasons without introducing a new argument. Use the structure as a model; write
about an experience of your own.
What two reasons support the main idea? Explain one example.
